baseline.name: Store and sort all observed stream values after every add
baseline.approach: Append each value, sort the growing collection and read its kth largest.
baseline.time: O(N log N) per add at current stream length N for comparison sorting
baseline.space: O(N) stored values plus sort workspace

archived.name: Min-heap retaining only the largest k values
archived.time: Construction O(n log(k+1)) for n initial values; add O(log(k+1)) worst case and O(1) when a full heap rejects a smaller value
archived.space: O(k) stored heap plus O(log(k+1)) recursive helper depth

why: Values below a full heap's root cannot enter the top k and can be discarded immediately.
quantitative_comparison: Storage is k heap slots instead of N stream values. An accepted heap insertion/replacement follows one heap path of depth at most floor(log2(k)); a full heap can reject a small value in constant work. Sorting-based work grows with all N values. No fixed elapsed-time factor follows.
tradeoffs: Only the requested rank is retained, not the full stream. k must be positive and enough values must exist before the root denotes a kth-largest value; allocations are unchecked.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
